prompt: Which step turns a model's scores for the next word into probabilities?
hint: Raise *e* to each score, then divide by the total.

choices.text: Softmax
choices.why: Right: everything then adds up to one.

choices.text: Top-k, which keeps the likeliest few and drops the rest
choices.why: Top-k cuts a distribution that softmax already produced.

choices.text: The tokenizer
choices.why: It splits text into tokens; it scores nothing.

choices.text: The temperature, by itself
choices.why: Temperature divides the scores; softmax still has to turn them into probabilities.

prompt: `on` scores 3.1 and `delayed` 2.6. At temperature 1, about how many times likelier is `on`? Give two decimal places.
hint: *e* to the power of the difference.

prompt: `purple` has a probability of 0.1% and was never drawn in 1,000 tries. What follows?
hint: Scale it up.

choices.text: It is never drawn, since the sampler ignores candidates under 1%
choices.why: Nothing in plain sampling drops a candidate for being small.

choices.text: The probability shown is wrong
choices.why: A thousand draws is a small sample of a 0.1% event.

choices.text: At a million calls it comes out about a thousand times
choices.why: Right: rare per call is not rare per day.

choices.text: Sampling is broken for the tail
choices.why: It is working as arithmetic says it should.

prompt: Adding 10 to every score leaves the probabilities exactly as they were. Why?
hint: What does softmax respond to?

choices.text: Softmax only uses the order of the scores
choices.why: The size of the gaps matters too, which is why temperature works.

choices.text: Only the differences between scores matter
choices.why: Right: a constant added to all of them cancels out.

choices.text: Scores above 10 are capped before softmax sees them
choices.why: Nothing is capped.

choices.text: Softmax divides every score by the largest one first
choices.why: It divides by the total of the exponentials.

prompt: What does a temperature below 1 do to the distribution?

choices.text: It flattens it so that the less likely words get drawn more often than before
choices.why: That is a temperature above 1.

choices.text: It sharpens it towards the top candidate
choices.why: Right: the gaps between scores are stretched.

choices.text: It removes the bottom half of the words
choices.why: Removing is what top-k and top-p do.

choices.text: Nothing until it reaches 0
choices.why: 0.2 changed `on` from 45.1% to 92.2%.

prompt: At temperature 1.5, what percentage did `pl sample` give `on`?
hint: The first line of the 1.5 run.

prompt: `pl sample` refuses a temperature of 0, while `pl run` uses 0 by default. Why is that consistent?
hint: What does the formula do with the temperature?

choices.text: `pl run` silently rounds 0 up to 0.1
choices.why: At 0 the stand-in takes the top score; nothing is rounded.

choices.text: 0 is the limit, the top candidate with no draw, and `pl sample` exists to show a draw
choices.why: Right: dividing by zero is undefined, so 0 is defined as the limit.

choices.text: Temperature 0 only exists for classification
choices.why: It exists for any task; it is a setting of the sampler.

choices.text: They use different samplers
choices.why: Both use `distribution` in `sample.py` above 0.

prompt: At temperature 0 the sampler takes the ___ candidate every time, with no draw at all.
hint: The one with the highest score.

prompt: Why does a temperature of 1 not promise the same amount of randomness on two different models?
hint: What is the temperature divided into?

choices.text: Providers define 1 differently in their price lists
choices.why: Prices have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Temperature is weaker on text in languages other than English
choices.why: It acts on scores, whatever the language of the text.

choices.text: It divides scores, and how far apart they sit differs
choices.why: Right: in the stand-in they sit within a point, so 1 is a lot.

choices.text: One of them ignores the setting and uses its own default
choices.why: Providers apply it; the point is the scale of the scores.

prompt: With `--top-p 0.9`, `lost` was kept along with the top three. Why?
hint: Add up the top three.

choices.text: Top-p always keeps four words
choices.why: A fixed count is top-k; top-p keeps a share.

choices.text: Three made only 86.1%
choices.why: Right: short of 90%, so the fourth joins.

choices.text: `lost` has a score above 1
choices.why: `ready` scores 1.0 and was cut; the threshold is a share, not a score.

choices.text: 0.9 rounds up to four candidates
choices.why: Nothing is rounded; the probabilities are added up.

prompt: With `--top-k 3`, what percentage did `on` get after renormalising?
hint: 45.1% divided by the share the three kept.

prompt: In a distribution where the top word has 97% of the probability, how many words do `top-k 3` and `top-p 0.9` keep?
hint: One is a count, the other a share.

choices.text: Three each
choices.why: Top-p stops as soon as the share is reached.

choices.text: Top-k keeps three; top-p keeps one
choices.why: Right: 97% is already past 90%.

choices.text: Top-k keeps one; top-p keeps three
choices.why: Top-k keeps its count whatever the shares.

choices.text: Both keep the words whose share is above the 3% that the top word left over
choices.why: Neither works by a per-word threshold.

prompt: Put the lab sampler's steps in the order it applies them.
hint: `distribution` in `sample.py`.
items: Softmax of the scores divided by the temperature
Keep the smallest top set reaching p
Renormalise what is left and draw

prompt: `--top-p 0.9` kept four words at temperature 1 and five at temperature 1.5. Why?
hint: Which step runs first?

choices.text: Temperature ran first and flattened it
choices.why: Right: a setting's effect depends on what ran before it.

choices.text: Top-p is applied before temperature
choices.why: The source shows temperature first.

choices.text: 1.5 adds a word to whatever top-p keeps
choices.why: Temperature adds nothing directly; it reshapes the probabilities.

choices.text: It was sampling noise, and a rerun would keep four
choices.why: Which words are kept is computed, not drawn.

prompt: Which of these accepts `temperature` and `top_p` but has no `top_k`?
hint: The section names two hosted APIs.

choices.text: Anthropic's Messages API
choices.why: It accepts all three.

choices.text: The lab's `pl sample`
choices.why: It has `--top-k` as well.

choices.text: OpenAI's Chat Completions API
choices.why: Right, which is why you read the documentation of the API you call.

choices.text: `pl run` with `--set`
choices.why: `--set top_k=…` is accepted.

prompt: Over 350 calls, right categories numbered 280 at temperature 0. How many at temperature 1?
hint: The `category` line of `pl check runs/t1.jsonl`.

prompt: The `json` line stayed at 340 at temperatures 0, 0.2 and 1. Why?
hint: What decides the stand-in's formatting habits?

choices.text: Temperature never affects formatting, in any model
choices.why: That is a claim about real models the lesson does not make.

choices.text: The prompt asks for JSON, which overrides the temperature
choices.why: The categories did change, so the temperature was not overridden.

choices.text: Coincidence
choices.why: Three identical counts are not chance here; there is a rule.

choices.text: In the stand-in, habits hang on the prompt and the message
choices.why: Right: they are not drawn by the sampler.

prompt: A team routes support tickets at temperature 0.3, "for a little flexibility". What does this lesson's measurement suggest?
hint: What happened at 0.2?

choices.text: Nothing changes below 0.5
choices.why: At 0.2 the categories already lost 9 of 280.

choices.text: Close calls flip from call to call; a task with one right answer belongs at 0
choices.why: Right: flexibility in routing is the same ticket going to two queues.

choices.text: They should raise it to 1 to see more variety
choices.why: At 1 the stand-in lost 86 of 280 right categories.

choices.text: 0.3 is fine as long as top-p is also set, so that the unlikely labels are cut off
choices.why: Top-p cuts the tail; close calls are at the top.

prompt: A hosted model at temperature 0 gives a different category for the same message once in a while. What is the likeliest explanation?
hint: What does the provider's own documentation say about 0?

choices.text: The temperature setting was ignored by the provider for that call
choices.why: It was applied; 0 is just not fully deterministic there.

choices.text: Batching and floating-point arithmetic swap near-ties
choices.why: Right: zero is not a guarantee of identical output.

choices.text: The model learnt from the previous call
choices.why: A call does not change the model.

choices.text: The message was cached the first time and the cache returned a stale category
choices.why: A prompt cache stores processed input, not answers.

prompt: For which of these is a temperature above 0 a reasonable choice? Choose all that apply.
hint: Does the task have one right answer?

choices.text: Five subject lines for a newsletter, to pick one from
choices.why: Yes: five identical lines would be useless.

choices.text: Sorting messages into five categories
choices.why: One right answer: keep it at 0.

choices.text: Drafting replies that should not all read alike
choices.why: Yes: variety is the point there.

choices.text: Sampling several answers on purpose to vote on them
choices.why: Yes: lesson 19 uses the randomness instead of suffering it.

prompt: Match each setting to what it did to *Your parcel is ___*.
hint: One each.

pairs.right: Nearly every draw was the top word

right_distractors: Writing stopped at 90% of the cap

prompt: In the lab you run with `--set temperature=0 --set top_p=0.5`. What does the top-p setting change?
hint: Is there a draw at temperature 0?

choices.text: Nothing: at 0 the top label is taken with no draw
choices.why: Right. Top-p only matters when something is drawn.

choices.text: It halves the labels it may choose from
choices.why: Nothing is chosen from a set at 0; the top is taken.

choices.text: It makes the answers more random
choices.why: Top-p only ever removes candidates.

choices.text: It overrides the temperature
choices.why: Temperature is applied first.
